title: Set up Hermes3D dev environment with interactive 3D viewer

title: 3D office visual overhaul: cinematic renderer, PBR materials, post-processing
body: ## Summary Complete visual overhaul of the immersive 3D office, aiming for a dramatically more realistic, cinematic look while staying smooth in the browser. ### Renderer core - Upgraded `three` 0.183 → 0.185, `@react-three/fiber` → 9.7, `@react-three/drei` → 10.7.8; added `@react-three/postprocessing`. - Switched the overview camera from orthographic to a cinematic perspective camera (40° FOV). Legacy orthographic zoom presets are auto-converted to equivalent perspective distances, so every existing fly-to preset keeps its framing. - ACES filmic tone mapping, PCF shadows at 2048–4096 with a softening radius and tight frustum. ### Lighting and atmosphere - Bundled CC0 HDRI sky (Poly Haven, 1.2 MB) for image-based lighting plus a visible sky. - Physically-plausible rig: warm key sun, cool sky fill, hemisphere bounce, and a slow daylight drift that keeps the scene alive without fighting the sky. - Distance fog and a vast horizon ground plane so the office sits on land instead of floating. ### Materials - New procedural PBR texture library (wood planks, plaster, concrete, carpet, brushed metal, fabric, grass) generated at runtime on canvas — zero bundled image assets, zero licensing exposure. - Full material sweep across environment, furniture, machines, kitchen, agents: Lambert/flat colors → textured Standard/Physical materials, glass panels, emissive screens/LEDs/neon tuned for bloom. ### Post-processing - N8AO ambient occlusion, mipmap bloom, SMAA, vignette, ACES tone mapping in the composer; depth of field in follow-cam mode on Ultra. ### Performance - New graphics quality presets (Low / Balanced / Ultra) in Studio Settings, persisted in localStorage, gating shadow resolution, post effects and max DPR. - Existing adaptive DPR controller preserved and parametrized. ## Testing - `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (same baseline as `main`), unit tests, production build. - Live browser verification with screenshots across overview, zoom, follow-cam and edit modes.

title: Single Hermes floor, Hermes agent task board, and white-screen fix
body: ## What changed Four changes: remove the multi-floor feature, rebuild the kanban as a Hermes-agent-native board (with no skill gate), and fix both the white screen on refresh and the "Maximum update depth exceeded" render cascades. ### Single Hermes floor - The office now has exactly one floor — **Hermes**. The floor registry (`src/lib/office/floors.ts`) collapses to a single definition; any persisted legacy floor id (`lobby`, `hermes-first`, `training`, …) is coerced onto it. - Deleted the "Building Directory" navigation HUD (`OfficeFloorNav`), the Prev/Next floor cycling, the lobby auto-navigate-on-connect flow, the floor-switch reconnect machinery, and the per-floor roster cache module. - The demo and real Hermes gateways are still both available — the adapter is chosen in settings/connect, not by walking between floors. ### Hermes agent task board (no skill gate) The kanban board mirrors the [Hermes agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) lifecycle and opens directly — task management is built into the Hermes agent, so the "Kanban Skill Not Installed" gate, the `task-manager` marketplace skill, and its packaged assets are all removed. The `tasks.json` format now lives in `docs/task-board.md`. | Column | Meaning | |---|---| | Inbox | Requests captured from any platform (Telegram, Discord, Slack, CLI…) | | Scheduled | Queued by the cron scheduler / playbooks, with due time | | Working | The agent is actively executing | | Needs Attention | Command approvals, questions, and errors | | Done | Finished — with a "☤ skill" badge when the learning loop produced a new skill | - Cards carry Hermes metadata: source platform, model used (e.g. `hermes-4-405b`), skills used/created, subagents spawned, schedule time, and a learned-skill flag — editable in the details pane and rendered as chips on cards. - Agent run phases map onto the lifecycle automatically: run start → Working, error/approval wait → Needs Attention, run end → Done; cron playbooks land in Scheduled. - Legacy statuses (`todo`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `review`) are accepted everywhere (API, file store, gateway events, settings mirror) and normalized, so existing `tasks.json` files keep working. ### White screen on refresh - The intermittent "Application error" page was renderer startup/context failure with no error boundary. The canvas is now wrapped in a retrying `SceneErrorBoundary`, lost WebGL contexts recover, and software rasterizers are detected with a throwaway probe **before** the canvas mounts so weak machines boot straight into the Low graphics preset. ### "Maximum update depth exceeded" cascades Long-session soak testing surfaced React nested-update storms with rotating blame. Root causes found and fixed: - `officeAnimationState` used a raw `Date.now()` as a memo dependency, giving every hold map a new identity on **every render** — all downstream effects re-fired per render, so any burst could snowball. Now snapped to a coarse 500ms clock. - The full WebGL canvas remounted on roster size / gateway status / camera-signal changes (`canvasResetKey`), producing mount storms; it now remounts only when the remote-office toggle changes the world footprint. - The gym-cooldown effect mutated a ref inside its setState updater, which flip-flopped under StrictMode's double-invocation. - The 4s task-store poll dispatched new card objects for every stored card on every poll; merges now bail on field-level equality, and `syncCardWithLinkedRun` returns the same reference when nothing changed. - The 250ms roster sync and janitor prune intervals moved to the transition lane so periodic cosmetic updates can never trip the sync nested-update limit. Verified with three long browser soaks (2 + 8 + 8 minutes) on this VM: zero update-depth errors and zero context losses after the fixes. ## Screenshots [Office without floor navigation](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-a24ea56e-13e1-4c4f-9afd-2e7c56843780/artifacts?path=%2Fworkspace%2Fscreenshots-review-5%2F01-office-no-floor-panels-final.webp) [Hermes task board with lifecycle columns](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-a24ea56e-13e1-4c4f-9afd-2e7c56843780/artifacts?path=%2Fworkspace%2Fscreenshots-review-5%2F07-hermes-board.webp) [Card with model and skill chips](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-a24ea56e-13e1-4c4f-9afd-2e7c56843780/artifacts?path=%2Fworkspace%2Fscreenshots-review-5%2F09-card-chips.webp) ## Verification - `npm run typecheck` — passes. - `npm run lint` — 8 errors / 24 warnings, all pre-existing on `main` (baseline was 9/26). - `npm test` — 1064 passed; the same 3 failures exist on `main` (pre-existing, unrelated). - `npm run build` — succeeds. - Browser verification in demo mode: no floor panels; board opens directly with columns/fields/chips/badge/status moves confirmed; `task-manager` absent from the marketplace; 18+ minutes of soak testing with zero renderer or update-depth errors. To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

title: Explain Hermes endpoints that cannot serve the gateway protocol
body: ## Why Pointing the gateway URL at `wss://:9119` cannot work, and today it fails as an unexplained 13 second connect timeout with no hint about what to change. Port `9119` is the hermes-agent dashboard. I stood up a stand-in for it locally and confirmed all three failure modes: | URL shape | Result | | --- | --- | | bare root, as typically configured | `404` on the upgrade — websockets live under `/api/ws` | | `/api/ws`, no ticket | closed `4401` — off-loopback binds require a single-use 30s ticket | | `/api/ws` + valid ticket | connects, then speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 | That last row is the important one. Even with perfect credentials the endpoint answers with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0",...}` and never produces the `hello-ok` that Hermes3D's connect frame is waiting for, so no username, password, or token can rescue it. `wss://` against that port also fails earlier at TLS, since the dashboard serves plain HTTP and Tailscale only terminates TLS on 443/8443/10000. The working path is unchanged and already documented: `npm run hermes-adapter` speaks the Hermes3D gateway protocol on `18789` and reaches Hermes over the OpenAI-compatible HTTP API on `8642`. I verified that chain end to end against a stub API and got `hello-ok` with `adapterType: "hermes"`. ## What changed - **`src/lib/gateway/upstreamUrlDiagnostics.ts`** — static inspection of the upstream URL, flagging the hermes-agent dashboard port, the `/api/ws` JSON-RPC path, the OpenAI API port, and `wss://` aimed at a tailnet port Tailscale cannot terminate TLS on. Each finding carries the fix, not just the complaint. - **Connect screen** — renders findings inline as the URL is typed, so the mismatch shows up before a connect attempt is spent on it. - **`npm run doctor`** — reports the same findings. The doctor runs under plain node and cannot import TypeScript, so it carries a mirrored copy; a test pins the two implementations to identical output across a table of URLs. - **Docs** — `TUTORIAL.md` gains a troubleshooting entry for this specific dead end, including the note that the dashboard username/password belong to `HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_*` and are unrelated to Hermes3D. `docs/hermes-gateway.md` documents both remote topologies: adapter next to Hermes3D (only the Hermes HTTP API crosses the network) versus adapter next to Hermes behind Tailscale Serve. A `ui-alert-caution` token was added next to the existing `ui-alert-danger` so the new UI stays inside the guarded color palette rather than reaching for raw Tailwind hues. ## Verification - `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` all clean; no new lint findings in changed files. - 13 new tests. Full suite: 1077 passing, with 3 failures in `agentChatPanel-controls` and `agentFleetHydration` that reproduce on `main` with these changes stashed. - Confirmed the doctor output against the exact reported URL: ``` [WARN] Gateway hints: Port 9119 is the hermes-agent dashboard, which speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over /api/ws with single-use ticket auth. Hermes3D cannot talk to it. Hermes3D connects through its own adapter, not the hermes-agent dashboard. Run `npm run hermes-adapter` with HERMES_API_URL pointing at the Hermes OpenAI-compatible API (port 8642), then connect to the adapter on port 18789. ``` ## Note This is diagnostics only — it explains the failure rather than making port `9119` connectable. Talking to hermes-agent's JSON-RPC gateway natively would mean a new runtime provider that performs the cookie login, mints a ticket per connect, and translates JSON-RPC methods into the Hermes3D contract. Happy to scope that separately if you'd rather connect without running the adapter.

title: Connect directly to a hermes-agent backend with no adapter process
body:
## Why

Connecting Hermes3D to a remote Hermes over Tailscale meant running the standalone gateway adapter somewhere — on the laptop, or on the Hermes box. That was never a configuration problem that could be solved on either end: **hermes-agent has no server that speaks the Hermes3D gateway protocol.** Searching it for the handshake (`hello-ok`, `connect.challenge`) returns nothing; its WebSocket surfaces (`/api/ws`, `/api/pty`, `/api/console`, `/api/pub`, `/api/events`) are JSON-RPC 2.0 or raw bytes. Hermes3D inherited its protocol from OpenClaw, and hermes-agent never spoke it.

So the adapter was a permanent third process to host and supervise, purely to translate.

## What changed

Studio translates in-process instead. A new `hermes-agent` adapter type points at the backend's own `/api/ws`, and `gateway-proxy.js` substitutes a bridge for the upstream socket rather than forwarding frames to it.

The bridge presents the slice of the `ws` surface the proxy actually uses (`readyState`, `send`, `close`, `terminate`, and the open/message/close/error events), which kept the proxy diff to a branch — connect handling, rate limiting, and lifecycle are untouched.

| Hermes3D | hermes-agent |
|---|---|
| `chat.send` | `session.create` / `session.resume` + `prompt.submit` |
| `chat` delta/final events | `message.delta` / `message.complete` |
| `chat.abort` | `session.interrupt` |
| `chat.history` | `session.history` |
| `sessions.list` | `session.list` (real stored sessions appear in Studio) |
| `models.list` | `model.options` |
| `exec.approval.resolve` | `approval.respond` |

A hermes-agent backend is a single agent, so the fleet is synthesised as one entry and session keys map onto runtime sessions created or resumed on first use.

### Auth

The backend's session token goes on the query string. This is what keeps a **loopback-bound** server published through Tailscale Serve reachable without a login — a non-loopback bind reports `auth_required: true` and demands dashboard credentials instead, which is the failure this repo has hit before.

When the backend refuses, its reason now reaches the connect screen rather than being flattened into `Failed to connect to upstream gateway WebSocket`. Distinguishing a bad token from a gated bind is the entire diagnosis, so a generic message here costs real debugging time.

### Interaction with #7

The endpoint guardrails added in #7 reject port `9119` and the `/api/ws` path. For this adapter that is exactly the right destination, so those two rules stand down when `adapterType` is `hermes-agent`. The non-TLS tailnet port warning still fires for both adapters, because `wss://` against a port Tailscale does not terminate TLS on fails either way.

## Testing

- `tests/unit/hermesAgentBridge.test.ts` (new, 14 tests) drives the bridge against a fake hermes-agent JSON-RPC server: URL building, token placement, `hello-ok`, delta accumulation, prompt failure, abort, session listing, and graceful degradation when an optional upstream method is missing.
- `tests/unit/gatewayProxy.test.ts` gains a test asserting the bridge's own error survives to the browser.
- `tests/unit/upstreamUrlDiagnostics.test.ts` covers both the suppression and the warning that must survive it.

Typecheck and lint are clean. Suite is 1094 passing; the 3 failures in `agentChatPanel-controls` and `agentFleetHydration` are pre-existing and reproduce on a clean tree.

### Verified live

Against a real backend over Tailscale, through the full browser path into Studio's proxy: TLS negotiated, `/api/ws` reached, and the backend's auth challenge surfaced with its actionable message. Chat, sessions, history, streaming, abort, models, and approvals are implemented against the mapped contract.

**Untested against a live backend:** cron, skills, and tasks are wired to hermes-agent's equivalents but were not exercised end to end.

## Test plan

- [ ] Set `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` on the backend and pin it so it survives restarts
- [ ] Set adapter type to `hermes-agent`, URL to the server root, token to that value
- [ ] Confirm connect succeeds with no adapter process on either machine (port 18789 free)
- [ ] Send a message and confirm streaming, then abort mid-turn
- [ ] Confirm `npm run doctor` reports no false positives for this adapter

title: Document the adapter-free hermes-agent setup over Tailscale
body:
## Summary

The direct `hermes-agent` path (#8, #9) shipped without a setup guide, so reproducing it meant rediscovering which port to bind, which token to use, and why the existing dashboard can't be reused. This adds `docs/hermes-agent-tailscale.md` and links it from the README, the tutorial, and the gateway doc.

The guide is built around the details that are easy to get wrong:

- **Bind loopback.** A public bind switches on the login gate, which rejects `?token=` entirely and demands a browser-minted ticket. `hermes serve --help` gives the same advice.
- **Pin the token.** Unset, `hermes serve` generates a random one per start, so a saved Studio profile silently breaks on the next restart.
- **Pick a free Tailscale Serve port.** A busy `443` surfaces as an opaque `401` rather than anything pointing at the real cause.
- **Keep it running.** launchd and systemd units are included, since the backend dying with its terminal is what sends people looking for this page in the first place.

Also corrects `docs/hermes-gateway.md`, which still claimed no native Studio-side provider existed.

## Verification

Checked against a real backend rather than assumed:

- A pinned `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` authenticates a WebSocket upgrade; a wrong token is refused with HTTP `403`.
- The token resolves through `~/.hermes/.env` via the CLI startup path — an earlier draft claimed the opposite and was corrected after testing.
- The gated-dashboard behaviour is confirmed live: `/api/auth/providers` reports the password provider, and `/api/auth/ws-ticket` returns `401` unauthenticated.

Docs only — no source changes.

title: Make the office react to conversations held in other clients
body:
## Summary

Hermes3D is a visualiser, not a chat client. When you talk to your agents in the desktop app, the TUI, or the CLI, the office had no way to know it happened — message events on the JSON-RPC gateway reach only the client that submitted the prompt, so an office watching from outside sees session activity but never the text.

This closes the gap with an **optional, user-installable plugin** rather than by pulling chat into Hermes3D:

- `plugins/hermes3d-office-bridge` observes finished turns via `post_llm_call` and republishes them on the backend's event bus. Observation only — no tool, no prompt-token cost, and it cannot delay or alter a turn. Plugins are scoped per `HERMES_HOME`, so `install.sh` covers the default home and every profile.
- The Studio bridge subscribes to that bus and relays turns as `office.speech`, which lands in the office feed and drives the huddle logic that already exists.
- [`docs/office-conversation-bridge.md`](docs/office-conversation-bridge.md) documents install, the data flow, what you see, config, and troubleshooting.

Three bugs the live runs surfaced, all fixed here:

- The office sampled only the **newest** feed reply, so agents answering the same group message within one render were dropped and no group ever formed.
- Group bookkeeping could leave an agent in **two overlapping huddles**, handing it two circles and leaving it walking between them forever. Reconciliation is now an explicit rule extracted into `reconcileConversationGroups` and unit tested.
- At 2.2x walk speed an agent on the far side of the 1800-unit floor was still walking a minute after the chat it was answering.

Also gates huddle speech bubbles on the speaking turn — standing in a circle everyone holds the same reply, and the bubbles overlapped into an unreadable stack.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean.
- [x] `npm run lint` — no new errors (the 6 in `RetroOffice3D.tsx` are pre-existing).
- [x] `npm run test -- --run` — 29 new tests; the 3 failures are pre-existing and identical on the base commit.
- [x] Live end-to-end against a real `hermes serve` backend: publishing three agent turns onto the event bus forms one group of three, and all three walk over and stand in the circle facing each other, with the bubble rotating between them.

title: Make the office bridge plugin work under profiles and one-shot turns
body:
## Summary

Installing the plugin from #12 on a real machine surfaced two paths where a turn was observed but the frame never reached the office.

- **Profiles couldn't see the token.** Each profile gets its own `HERMES_HOME` and its own `.env`, so a profile-scoped turn never saw a `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` pinned in the default home, and the plugin disabled itself at register time. That token isn't profile-level config — it identifies the one local dashboard every profile publishes to — so it now falls back to the default home's `.env` rather than asking users to copy the same secret into every profile.
- **One-shot turns were lost.** The sender is a daemon thread, so `hermes -z` ended its process while the frame was still queued and the socket wasn't open yet. title: Stop the office token from breaking the Hermes desktop app
body:
## Summary

Following our own bridge guide made the Hermes desktop app unlaunchable:

```
Local Hermes backend is HTTP-reachable but the WebSocket (/api/ws)
rejected the session token: WebSocket connection failed.
```

The guide said to pin `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` in `~/.hermes/.env` so the office backend keeps a stable token. Hermes loads that file with `override=True`, so the pin lands on **every** backend the machine starts — including the one the desktop app spawns. The app mints a fresh token per launch, passes it to its child, then probes `/api/ws` with it; the pin overrode the child's token, the probe failed, and the app died at boot.

The fix is a dedicated name. `HERMES3D_OFFICE_TOKEN` is pinned in `.env` and passed to the office backend inline on its command line, which `.env` cannot override because the pinned name differs. Every other backend keeps minting its own.

- The resolver does **not** fall back to the process's own `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` — that authenticates whichever backend the plugin is running inside, rarely the one it publishes to, so reading it would send a wrong token and fail silently. Existing setups are covered by reading the pinned file.
- The installer warned when the dashboard token was *absent*, pushing users into the trap. It now warns when it is *present* and shows the rename.
- Both docs get the warning, and the launchd/systemd units read the token out of `.env` at launch so it stays out of service definitions and `ps`.

## Test plan

- [x] A backend spawned the way the desktop app spawns its own accepts the token it minted (the exact `/api/ws` probe that was failing).
- [x] A profile-scoped one-shot turn still publishes to the office backend end to end.
- [x] Token precedence: office token wins; the desktop backend's token is never used.

## Summary

When a group message went out and every agent replied, all four bubbles rendered at once into an unreadable stack, and the huddle circle was loose enough that members overlapped each other and came to rest inside desks.

## Summary

Clicking the kanban desk on a hermes-agent connection showed "Kanban Skill Not Installed — install the TASK-MANAGER skill". That gate belongs to the legacy backend, where task tracking is a skill that writes a JSON file. Kanban is **built into hermes-agent** — every `hermes serve` exposes the board at `/api/plugins/kanban/*` on the same origin and session token the gateway already uses. The office now shows that board with nothing to install.

- **Read**: the bridge's `tasks.list` (previously hardcoded `{tasks: []}`) fetches `GET /board` and maps hermes tasks onto office cards — `kanban:` id prefix, epoch-seconds → ISO, and the nine hermes statuses collapsed onto the five office columns (`triage/todo → Inbox`, `scheduled/ready → Scheduled`, `running → Working`, `blocked/review → Needs attention`, `done/archived → Done`).

- **Honest adapter identity**: the bridge's hello now announces `adapterType: "hermes-agent"` and the client accepts it — detection previously downgraded every bridge connection to `"hermes"`, which is exactly why the skill gate fired. title: Improve adaptive mobile rendering performance
body:
## Summary
- choose the existing Low renderer tier automatically for constrained mobile/coarse-pointer devices, reduced-motion users, and software WebGL while preserving explicit user overrides
- reduce Low-tier GPU work by capping DPR at 1, disabling framebuffer MSAA, dynamic shadows, and decorative particles
- pause the scene simulation tick while the document is hidden
- keep Balanced and Ultra desktop defaults visually unchanged

## Problem and profiling
A real phone can render the office, but the current default is not responsive enough. Profiling first showed the existing renderer already had quality presets and adaptive DPR, so this patch extends those mechanisms rather than adding a separate mobile renderer or UA sniffing.

The reproducible comparison used clean production builds from the same `main` revision and route, Chromium's 412×915 mobile profile at DPR 3, and SwiftShader. It is a constrained software-renderer proxy, not a real-phone benchmark. Results are one matched checkpoint and should be treated as directional rather than statistically conclusive.

| Metric | `main` | this branch | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| drawing buffer | 515×1143 (588,645 px) | 412×915 (376,980 px) | -36.0% pixels |
| sampled FPS | 1.83 | 2.46 | +34.0% |
| median sampled frame interval | 33.4 ms | 16.7 ms | -50.0% |
| used JS heap after capture | 66.9 MB | 48.4 MB | -27.6% |
| production network transfer | 5.10 MB | 5.10 MB | unchanged |

Long-task results were noisy and did not improve reliably, so this PR makes no long-task claim. The profile was not capable of trustworthy GPU/draw-call/triangle or thermal measurements. Real-device validation remains required.

## Root causes addressed
- mobile/coarse-pointer hardware previously defaulted to Balanced unless it exposed a software renderer
- Low still rendered at DPR 1.25 with MSAA, a 1024 shadow map, and per-frame dust animation
- the scene simulation tick did not explicitly guard hidden documents

## Behavior and compatibility
- no UA sniffing; selection uses viewport width, coarse-pointer media query, `deviceMemory` when available, reduced-motion preference, and the existing WebGL renderer probe
- a stored Low/Balanced/Ultra choice always wins over automatic selection
- Balanced and Ultra retain their prior DPR, shadows, post-processing, and decorative motion
- changing quality remounts the canvas so immutable WebGL context options apply correctly
- no gateway/API changes and no bundled asset changes

## Testing
- [x] `npm run test -- --run` — 180 files, 1,190 tests passed
- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors; 9 pre-existing warnings
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] focused quality tests — automatic desktop/mobile/reduced-motion selection, stored override, DPR bounds, hidden pause
- [x] sanitized 412×915 production mobile smoke on baseline and branch
- [x] screenshot output dimensions matched (1236×2745 at DPR 3); visual delta was bounded to quality reduction (normalized RMSE 0.074)

## Risks and rollback
Low intentionally trades soft shadows, MSAA, and dust motes for responsiveness. Users can select Balanced or Ultra in the existing graphics setting. Reverting commit `9a43734` fully restores prior behavior.

## Remaining validation
- real-phone median/p95 frame time, long tasks, thermal behavior, and interaction smoke
- maintainer visual review of the Low-tier tradeoff on representative phones
- desktop screenshot smoke on physical GPU (desktop configuration is unchanged)

title: [BUG] TypeScript 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')' in office when skillsReport contains entries missing name/skillKey
body:
---
name: Bug report
about: Create a report to help us improve
title: "[BUG] TypeScript 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '\''trim'\'')' in office when skillsReport contains entries missing name/skillKey"
labels: bug
assignees: ''
---

**Describe the bug**

The office screen crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')` whenever the connected Hermes backend's skills report contains a skill entry where `skillKey` or `name` is `undefined`. The kanban/task-manager detection and the marketplace enable paths call `.trim()` unconditionally on those fields, so a single field-less entry breaks the whole office UI (React error overlay).

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Start Hermes3D and connect to a real Hermes backend whose `skillsReport` includes at least one skill without a `skillKey` / `name` field (or run the demo gateway with a crafted skills payload).
2. Open the office screen (`/office`).
3. Observe the Kanban desk / task-manager detection component render cycle.
4. See the error overlay: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')`.

**Expected behavior**

Skill entries with missing `name` / `skillKey` should be handled gracefully (treated as empty string, skipped by keyword matching) instead of crashing the office UI.

**Root cause**

Three call sites assume every skill entry has string `skillKey` / `name`:

- `src/features/office/screens/OfficeScreen.tsx` — `soundhermesSkill` and `taskManagerSkill` detection:
  ```ts
  const normalizedKey = skill.skillKey.trim().toLowerCase();   // crash if skillKey undefined
  const normalizedName = skill.name.trim().toLowerCase();      // crash if name undefined
  ```
- `src/features/office/hooks/useOfficeSkillsMarketplace.ts` — `handleSetSkillEnabled`:
  ```ts
  (skill) => skill.name.trim() === skillName.trim(),           // crash if name undefined
  ```

**Proposed fix** (minimal, safe-guards all three):

```ts
// OfficeScreen.tsx
const normKey = (skill: { skillKey?: string; name?: string }) =>
  (skill.skillKey ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();
const normName = (skill: { skillKey?: string; name?: string }) =>
  (skill.name ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();
```
And use `normKey(skill)` / `normName(skill)` in both `find` callbacks.

```ts
// useOfficeSkillsMarketplace.ts
(skill) => (skill.name ?? "").trim() === skillName.trim(),
```

**Screenshots**

n/a (error overlay text: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')` over the Kanban desk panel).

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Browser: Chromium (Hermes desktop preview pane)
 - Hermes3D version / commit: main (166b4f2 / 23 commits as of 2026-08-26)
 - Build method: source (`npm run dev`)

**Additional context**

Observed against a self-hosted Hermes Agent gateway (hermes-gateway-adapter). The Hermes `skills` payload includes entries whose schema doesn't guarantee `name`/`skillKey` on every item; the frontend must not assume them.

Local tested fix confirms the office screen renders and the Kanban desk loads once the guards are in place.

title: fix: allow WebAssembly compilation in production CSP
body:
## Problem

In a production build (`npm run build && npm run start`), the CSP drops `'unsafe-eval'` entirely — but a three.js chunk (draco/basis decoder preload) calls `WebAssembly.instantiate` during module evaluation. The whole chunk dies with a `CompileError` and dependent UI never renders. Observed symptom: agent roster stuck empty on production while `npm run dev` works fine (dev's `'unsafe-eval'` covers WASM, which is why it never reproduces there).

```
CompileError: WebAssembly.instantiate(): ... violates the following Content Security Policy
directive because 'unsafe-eval' is not an allowed source of script:
"script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' blob:"
```

## Fix

Add `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` to the production `script-src`. It only permits WASM compilation — JS `eval` stays blocked, so the production hardening intent is preserved. Dev mode unchanged.

## Verification

Reproduced on a production build connected to a custom gateway (12-agent fleet): before the fix the chunk errored on load; after rebuild the console is clean and the office renders fully.

title: fix: recover agent fleet hydration when demo placeholder is seeded before connect
body:
## Problem

With the demo adapter selected, the disconnected-state effect in `OfficeScreen.tsx` seeds a local **"Main"** placeholder agent and sets `agentsLoaded = true`. If the (auto-)connect lands a moment later:

- the connected effect (`if (status !== "connected" || agentsLoaded) return`) skips hydration, and
- the retry effect requires `state.agents.length === 0`, which is now 1.

So the office stays stuck on the lone "Main" placeholder even though the gateway is healthy — `agents.list` through the Studio proxy returns the full fleet. The race is timing-dependent: dev builds usually connect before the seed wins, while production builds render faster and hit it reliably (repro: production build + a gateway on the default `ws://localhost:18789`, demo backend selected → "demo • connected" with 1 agent).

## Fix

When connected and the fleet is still exactly the placeholder (`length === 1 && agents[0].id === MAIN_AGENT_ID`), force one reload per connection. Guarded by a ref reset on disconnect so a gateway that genuinely serves a single `main` agent doesn't re-trigger in a loop.

## Verification

On the reproducing setup (production build, 12-agent custom gateway): before the fix the office showed 1 placeholder agent while a direct WS probe through `/api/gateway/ws` returned 12; after the fix the full fleet hydrates on first load.

title: /office screen never attempts a connection — stuck on "Connecting to your runtime..." indefinitely, reproducible with the bundled demo gateway (zero config)
body:
**Title:** `/office` screen never attempts a connection — stuck on "Connecting to your runtime..." indefinitely, reproducible with the bundled demo gateway (zero config)

**Summary**

The `/office` screen never initiates a WebSocket connection at all, regardless of which backend provider is configured. It's not a failed connection — it's a connection that's never attempted. Reproduced with a real `hermes-agent` backend and, separately, with the bundled zero-dependency demo gateway, with identical results both times.

**Environment**

- Hermes3D: fresh clone, `next` bumped to `16.3.4` (from `16.1.7`) to clear `npm audit` findings — unrelated to this bug, mentioning for completeness
- Node 22.23.1 / npm 10.9.8, macOS
- Ran via `npm run dev`, both `hermes-agent` and `demo` adapter types tested

**Steps to reproduce (demo gateway — no external backend needed)**

1. `npm install && cp .env.example .env`
2. `npm run demo-gateway` (confirmed listening on `ws://localhost:18789`)
3. In `.env`: `HERMES3D_GATEWAY_URL=ws://localhost:18789`, `HERMES3D_GATEWAY_ADAPTER_TYPE=demo`
4. `npm run dev`, open `http://localhost:3000/office`
5. The office screen shows "Connecting to your runtime..." and never progresses, even after several minutes.

**Root cause (traced, not guessed)**

1. **The top-level gateway config resolves correctly.** `GET /api/studio` returns `localGatewayDefaults` matching whatever `.env` says (confirmed for both `demo` and `hermes-agent` adapter types) — the env-var wiring described in the README's Quick Start works as documented, up to this point.
2. **The `/office` screen never opens a socket.** Proxied `window.WebSocket`'s constructor before any page script ran, then waited 8s on a loaded `/office` page: zero WebSocket connections logged. This rules out a failed handshake — the app isn't trying at all.
3. **The screen reads from a different config entirely.** `GET /api/studio` also returns `settings.officeFloors.<activeFloorId>`, which is seeded independently of the top-level `gateway` block:
   ```json
   "officeFloors": {
     "hermes": {
       "floorId": "hermes",
       "provider": "hermes",
       "runtimeProfileId": "hermes-default",
       "gatewayUrl": null,
       "status": "disconnected"
     }
   }
   ```
   `provider: "hermes"` and `gatewayUrl: null` here, regardless of what `HERMES3D_GATEWAY_ADAPTER_TYPE`/`HERMES3D_GATEWAY_URL` are set to. Nothing appears to populate this floor's `gatewayUrl` from the top-level gateway settings.
4. **Confirmed this isn't specific to one adapter type.** Repeated the whole test with `HERMES3D_GATEWAY_ADAPTER_TYPE=hermes-agent` pointed at a real, verified-working `hermes serve` backend (confirmed the backend itself was reachable and correctly authenticating via a manual `WebSocket` test from the browser's own JS console — real `101 Switching Protocols` + a live `gateway.ready` event). `officeFloors.hermes` was byte-for-byte identical in both cases. Same stuck screen either way.

**Separately, for anyone using a loopback `hermes-agent` URL specifically:** `resolveStudioProxyGatewayUrl` (`src/lib/gateway/proxy-url.ts`) returns a loopback `HERMES3D_GATEWAY_URL` completely unchanged — no path, no token appended. The docs' "Studio appends the path itself" guidance only applies to the remote/Tailscale-proxied case (`/api/gateway/ws`); for a direct loopback connection, both the `/api/ws` path and the `?token=` query parameter have to be included in `HERMES3D_GATEWAY_URL` by hand, since the backend's WS route requires the token in the query string during the handshake itself (checked before any post-connect message could arrive). This alone doesn't explain the `/office` symptom above (still stuck even once wired correctly), but it's a real gap worth fixing or documenting either way.

**Expected behavior**

The `/office` screen connects using the gateway configured via `.env`/the connect screen, the same way the top-level settings already correctly resolve.

**What I haven't done**

Traced *where* a floor's `provider`/`gatewayUrl` is supposed to get assigned from the top-level settings — `studioBootstrapOperation.ts`, `useRuntimeConnection.ts`, and `RetroOffice3D.tsx` all reference floor `gatewayUrl` and looked like the most likely places, but I didn't follow it to a conclusion. Happy to share more detail (console logs, network captures, `/api/studio` responses) if useful.

title: feat(hermes-agent): show kanban workers as working agents
body:
## Problem

With the **Hermes Agent (direct)** backend, most unattended work happens as `hermes kanban` workers: the dispatcher claims a card and spawns a worker for the assignee profile. Those runs never go through the JSON-RPC gateway the office is connected to, so the office shows every character as idle (`0 working · N idle`) while agents are busy on cards.

## Change

The bridge now watches kanban workers and replays them as agent activity:

- New `server/hermes-agent/kanban-activity.js` polls the kanban plugin API the bridge already uses for the task desk: `GET /boards`, then `GET /workers/active?board=<slug>` only for boards reporting a running card.
- Each worker run maps onto the agent named after its `profile` (falling back to `task_assignee`). It emits the same `agent` lifecycle events a locally started chat produces: `start` when the run appears and `end` when it is gone. The run also gets one `office.speech` bubble, `Kanban: <card title>`.
- Session key `agent:<profile>:kanban:<board>:<task>:<run>` resolves through the existing `parseAgentIdFromSessionKey` fallback. Nothing changes on the client.

Behaviour details:

- **Read-only.** It never changes a card, a run or a board.
- **Failed polls are tolerated.** The previous snapshot is kept, so a restarting backend does not make the whole office stand up at once, and the same error is logged only once.
- **Late browsers still see live runs.** Runs that are already live are re-announced on every poll, so a browser that connects later still sees them. A repeated `start` for the same `runId` is a no-op in `resolveLifecyclePatch`.
- **Configurable.** `HERMES3D_KANBAN_ACTIVITY_INTERVAL_MS` sets the interval: 15000 by default, clamped to at least 2000, and `0` disables it.
- The watcher starts after `connect` once the roster is loaded, and stops on close or terminate, alongside the office-speech subscriber.

Docs: a short paragraph in `docs/hermes-agent-tailscale.md` next to the existing kanban desk section.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/hermesAgentKanbanActivity.test.ts` has 10 tests:
  - Unit tests for interval parsing, board filtering, the worker → agent mapping, the diff, and the watcher's start / still-active / end and failed-poll behaviour.
  - Two integration tests that run the real bridge against a fake backend serving `/api/ws` and `/api/plugins/kanban/*`. They check that the session token header is sent, and that nothing is polled when the watcher is disabled.
- `npx vitest run tests/unit/hermesAgentKanbanActivity.test.ts tests/unit/hermesAgentBridge.test.ts tests/unit/hermesAgentKanban.test.ts` → 50 passed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` on the touched files are clean.
- Full `vitest run` on Windows: `colorSemanticsGuard` and `gatewayMediaRoute › rejects symlinked local media paths` fail identically on `main` without this change. They are pre-existing and Windows-related, not touched here.

Manual check against a real hermes-agent 0.21.5 backend with 12 profiles and one board running a worker: the office went from `0 working · 12 idle` to `1 working · 11 idle`, and the assignee's character switched to working. It flipped back when the run ended and moved to the next agent the dispatcher spawned.

body:
## Summary

With a Hermes Agent backend (`hermes gateway` API server on :8642), several adapter features silently didn't work, because the API server runs its own toolset and ignores tools sent by the client. This PR wires them up. **It changes gateway adapter behavior** (`server/hermes-gateway-adapter.js`).

- **Agent instructions:** each agent's files (`IDENTITY/SOUL/AGENTS/TOOLS/USER/HEARTBEAT/MEMORY.md`, e.g. from the company builder) were stored but never sent to the model; agents only got `You are <name>.` They're now appended to the system prompt.
- **Persistence:** created agents, their files, and command modes were in memory only and vanished on restart. They're saved to `~/.hermes/hermes3d-agents.json`.
- **Delegation:** the orchestrator's `TEAM_TOOLS` never reached Hermes, so it used its own built-in subagents instead of the office agents. The adapter now also serves `list_team` / `delegate_task` / `read_agent_context` as a token-protected MCP endpoint at `/mcp` (`server/office-mcp.js`) that Hermes connects to via `mcp_servers`. Guards: a busy agent can't take a second task, no self-delegation, max 4 concurrent delegations.
- **Live activity:** `hermes.tool.progress` SSE events were dropped and no lifecycle events were sent, so the office looked frozen for minutes while an agent used tools. Tool progress and `lifecycle` start/end/error events are now forwarded.
- **No double runs:** `streamOneTurn` re-sent the request non-streaming whenever a stream ended without text. Against Hermes that reruns the whole agent turn, including any commands. The fallback now only applies when the server didn't stream at all.
- **Command modes and approvals:** `exec.approvals.get/set` were stubs, so off/ask/auto did nothing. The adapter now stores the modes and applies them to Hermes `approval.request` events: auto approves, ask shows the request in the office, off denies (and tells the agent not to run commands). Answers go to `POST /v1/runs/{id}/approval`.
- **Office approvals panel:** approval cards only existed on the Agents page, so an `ask` agent in `/office` waited with nothing to answer. Added `OfficeApprovalsPanel`; pending approvals are replayed when a page connects.
- **Docs:** `docs/hermes-gateway.md` covers the MCP setup and approvals (including that Hermes must use `approvals.mode: manual` for the per-agent modes to apply); `.env.example` gains `HERMES3D_MCP_TOKEN`.

I know the guidelines prefer small PRs. These pieces depend on each other (approvals need the stream parsing, delegation needs the agent prompts), but I'm happy to split it up if you'd prefer.

**Known limits:** Hermes only raises approvals for commands it flags as risky, so routine commands run without asking in every mode, and Hermes can't restrict tools per request, so `off` relies on the agent's instructions plus denial of anything flagged.

title: [BUG] Hermes approval requests are withdrawn: bridge doesn't advertise server_requests, and the Office has no approval UI
body:
**Describe the bug**

With the `hermes-agent` adapter, any action that needs approval (e.g. writing a protected file such as `AGENTS.md`) fails. Hermes reports: "approval was withdrawn… the attached client cannot answer approval requests (update the Hermes app)". Three causes:

1. The embedded bridge (`server/hermes-agent/bridge.js`) never sends `client.capabilities {server_requests: true}`, so Hermes treats the client as unable to answer approvals and withdraws the request.
2. `jsonrpc-client.js` doesn't handle server→client requests (frames carrying both `id` and `method`, such as `approval`), and the bridge has no handler for them. The legacy `approval.respond` path also mapped every decision except "allow" to deny.
3. Even with the server side fixed, no approval card appears. The approval UI is wired only in `AgentsPageScreen` (`/agents`), and `src/app/agents/page.tsx` redirects `/agents` to `/office`. `OfficeScreen` doesn't subscribe to `exec.approval.requested` or render the approval card.

**To Reproduce**
1. Run Hermes Agent (`hermes serve`) with a profile where `approvals.mode` is not `off`; connect Hermes3D to it.
2. Open `/office` and select an agent.
3. Ask the agent to edit a protected file, e.g. "Append a line to C:\path\AGENTS.md".
4. The agent reports the approval was withdrawn / timed out; no approval card appears.

**Expected behavior**
Hermes3D advertises the capability, turns the `approval` server request into an `exec.approval.requested` event, shows the card in the Office, and sends the user's choice (once / session / always / deny) back to Hermes.

**Environment**
 - Browser: Google Chrome
 - Hermes3D version / commit: beb7629
 - Build method: source (`npm run build` + `npm start`, `UPSTREAM_ALLOWLIST=localhost,127.0.0.1`)
 - OS: Windows; Hermes Agent running locally

**Additional context**
I have a patch (PR to follow). Verified locally against a real Hermes Agent: the card appears in the Office chat, "Allow once" lets the file write through, and "Deny" blocks it (file unchanged). "Always allow" was clicked once and the write succeeded; I did not verify how Hermes persists that choice.

title: fix: answer Hermes approval requests and show the approval card in the Office
body:
## Summary
- Advertise `client.capabilities {server_requests: true}` when the hermes-agent gateway is ready, so Hermes no longer withdraws approvals.

The legacy `approval.respond` path no longer turns every non-"allow" decision into deny.

body:
## Summary

Found and fixed a handful of real bugs in `server/hermes-gateway-adapter.js` while building and installing a packaged skill through the Marketplace against this adapter:

- **`skills.status` crashed marketplace installs.** It returned a stub with no `workspaceDir`, so `normalizeRequired(workspaceDir).trim()` threw on `undefined` partway through every install. Now resolves the real per-agent workspace and scans it for installed skills.
- **`config.get`/`config.set` were no-op stubs**, so the Marketplace's "enable skill for agent" allowlist state could never actually persist. Now backed by a real, adapter-local config store — deliberately a *separate* file from `~/.hermes/config.json`, so it never touches the real Hermes CLI's own config.
- **Marketplace installs silently no-op'd.** The install flow spins up a temporary installer agent and asks the model to write files via "file tools" that were never wired up (every non-orchestrator agent got `tools: []`), so the UI reported success while nothing was ever written. Added a deterministic installer that recognizes the installer's message format and writes the files directly instead of relying on the model to fake tool calls.
- **No agent except the orchestrator had any tools at all.** Added `read_file`/`write_file`/`list_directory`, sandboxed to each agent's own workspace (path-traversal guarded), available to every agent.
- **`delegate_task` was a strictly weaker capability than chatting directly** — it ran a bare completion with `tools: []` instead of the tool-enabled agentic loop. Now routes through the same loop as a direct chat turn.
- **Agent identity and the agent registry didn't survive a restart.** Only conversation history was persisted; a rename or a spawned agent vanished on every adapter restart. Both now persist to disk and reload on startup.
- **The orchestrator's real system prompt ignored its own profile files.** It was always a hardcoded generic string, even though the UI lets you edit `IDENTITY.md`/`SOUL.md`/`AGENTS.md`/`USER.md`/`HEARTBEAT.md` for it. Now the system prompt is actually built from those files, so a customized orchestrator persona takes effect in conversation, not just as a display label.
- **Temporary install/remove agents leaked as phantom office characters.** Cleaned up from the live registry when they drop out of the config-based agent list.

## Test plan

- [x] Installed a packaged skill end-to-end through the Marketplace UI and confirmed the file actually lands on disk at the agent's real workspace path
- [x] Confirmed `config.get`/`config.set` round-trip and the "enabled" state survives a page reload
- [x] Sent a real chat message to a non-orchestrator agent and confirmed `read_file`/`write_file`/`list_directory` tool calls execute and stay inside that agent's workspace (path-traversal attempt rejected)

title: Disable two unconditional, no-toggle audio sources in the office
body:
## Summary

Two separate synthesized-audio systems in the retro office play constantly during normal agent activity, with no settings toggle to turn either off:

1. **Huddle-chatter murmur** (`conversationChatterAudio.ts`, wired into `RetroOffice3D.tsx`) — synthesizes fake "speech" (short filtered triangle-wave blips, no real audio assets) whenever two or more agents are near each other conversing. Fires on every huddle, unconditionally.

2. **Messaging-booth sound effects** — the booth used for drafting WhatsApp/Telegram/phone-call content plays a synthesized key tone on every typed character, a two-tone ring, and can fetch and play real TTS voice audio via `/api/office/voice/reply`. All routed through one `getBoothAudioContext()` helper, also unconditional.

With any real multi-agent activity (agents coordinating, delegating, drafting messages), both fire constantly, and the synthesized-speech effect in particular reads as unsettling rather than ambient — this was reported to me directly as "too creepy, need to shut off."

## Changes

- `conversationChatterAudio`'s instantiation/wiring removed from `RetroOffice3D.tsx`. The class itself is untouched in case a muteable version is wanted later.
- `getBoothAudioContext()` now always resolves to `null`. Every caller (`playPhoneKeyTone`, `playTextKeyTone`, `playPhoneRingTone`, `playBoothVoice`) already early-returns on a null context, so this silences all four from one place without touching their call sites or behavior otherwise.

Both are minimal, targeted removals — no new settings UI, no behavior change outside the audio itself. Booth functionality (drafting, sending, the visible typing/composing UI) is unaffected; only the sound is gone.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean after each change
- [x] Dev server restart, triggered real huddle conversations and real booth drafting flows afterward — confirmed via network/console/DOM inspection that no audio-related activity fires (no `/api/office/voice/reply` requests, no `<audio>` elements, no AudioContext-related console output)
- [x] Confirmed silent by the person who originally reported the sound, after a hard reload
